name: From Bolivar to Lula: Latin America Since Independence
description: Two centuries of independence in Latin America: the wars that broke Spain and Portugal's hold, emperors and revolutions, populists, coups and debts, and the return of the vote.

checkpoints.name: The wars of liberation
checkpoints.note: The Haitian Revolution under Toussaint Louverture ends slavery and French rule. Miguel Hidalgo begins Mexico's war in 1810. Jose de San Martin crosses the Andes to free Chile with Bernardo O'Higgins and goes on to Peru, Simon Bolivar builds Gran Colombia, and Brazil breaks from Portugal in 1822.

checkpoints.name: Emperors and reformers
checkpoints.note: Mexico loses half its land in the Mexican-American War, and Benito Juarez leads it through reform and a French-backed empire. Paraguay is crushed in the War of the Triple Alliance. The Empire of Brazil ends slavery in 1888 and deposes Pedro II in 1889. Jose Marti dies fighting for Cuba in 1895.

checkpoints.name: Revolution and the masses
checkpoints.note: The Mexican Revolution brings Emiliano Zapata and Pancho Villa to the fore, and the party that becomes the PRI then rules Mexico for over seventy years. Diego Rivera and the Mexican muralists paint its story on public walls. The Panama Canal opens in 1914, and Getulio Vargas takes power in Brazil in 1930.

checkpoints.name: Populists and guerrillas
checkpoints.note: Juan Peron wins Argentina's presidency in 1946, and Eva Peron becomes the champion of its poor. Vargas returns and dies in office in 1954. Fidel Castro and Che Guevara lead the Cuban Revolution to victory in 1959, Brazil opens its new capital, Brasilia, in 1960, and Che is killed in Bolivia in 1967.

checkpoints.name: Coups and debts
checkpoints.note: Salvador Allende is elected in Chile in 1970 and dies in the Chilean coup of 1973, which brings Augusto Pinochet to power. Military rulers also hold Argentina, whose invasion of the Falklands in 1982 ends in defeat. That same year the Latin American debt crisis begins a lost decade of growth.

checkpoints.name: The vote returns
checkpoints.note: Pinochet hands power to an elected president in 1990, and Mexico's PRI loses the presidency in 2000. The Argentine crisis empties savings and topples governments around 2001. In Brazil the former union leader Lula da Silva is elected president in 2002 and returns to office in 2023.
